findings.title: Byte-bound rejection depends on an unspecified value representation
findings.observation: V makes 65,536 canonical UTF-8 bytes a semantic input/result/state bound, but supplies mathematical value types and JSON serialization rules without a normative embedding of each value, schema, input record and assembled state into JSON. Sorting keys and choosing escapes makes an existing JSON tree canonical; it does not choose that tree. In particular Collection<T,N>, Option<T>, numeric/indexed values and their type metadata have no exact object/array layout or explicit inherited schema mapping. The old candidate wire is not incorporated as the wire of this new, distinct contract.
findings.consequence: Two implementations can agree on every type, integer, expression equation and value-node count, yet disagree on input admission or VALUE_BOUND. Thus total finite-bound reduction and the phase/work/span of boundary failures are not fixed by the source. Deferring codec implementation is appropriate, but deferring the normative size function leaves this claimed complete expression contract underdetermined.

independentDiscriminator.representationA: schema-directed arrays of canonical UInt64 decimal strings, under record key r
independentDiscriminator.representationB: tagged Collection objects with elementType, capacity and items; tagged UInt64 objects with value, under r
independentDiscriminator.result: A fits and B exceeds the bound. These are illustrative source-compatible representation choices, not executions of a candidate codec.

findings.requiredChange: Define a total normative value/schema/state-to-canonical-JSON mapping, or a precise representation-independent byte-size function, including type metadata and aggregate wrappers. Bind descriptor aggregate sizing and synthetic-span representation where relevant. Add independently recomputed boundary examples and re-check finite-record-bound input admission. No production runtime or implemented wire codec is required for this correction.

designReasons.EX-D1: Strict left-to-right Bool operations make cost and failure ordering explicit. They are a coherent proposed choice; distinguish them from any future short-circuit source contract. The false-left division-by-zero case correctly costs six entries.
designReasons.EX-D2: Exact type indices, checked intermediates, Euclidean signed division and explicit Quantity unit/scale calculations prevent silent conversions. The checked product must reject before a parent quotient even if that quotient would fit. The absence of implicit Rate*Amount or rescaling must remain an open financial requirement where a target needs it, not removal of that target.
designReasons.EX-D3: An explicit pre/post read-view in the same constructor is unambiguous at the expression level; only Ensure conditions may select post, and next remains forbidden.
designReasons.EX-D4: One unit per entered node, no re-charge on resumption, and zero charge for a node that cannot enter form a deterministic local cost policy. Diagnostic work is not ledger authority; lifecycle charging remains open.
designReasons.EX-D5: Accessor aliases preserve names, semantics and node charges. Any optimizer removing a charge needs separate correspondence evidence.
designReasons.EX-D6: Typed ordered descriptors are a useful pure preparation interface. ExpressionPrepared explicitly grants no financial effect or settlement; operation/postcondition coupling remains an unresolved prerequisite for combined execution, not for specifying this layer.
designReasons.EX-D7: Finite simultaneous resource limits, byte spans and static-before-runtime admission are appropriate proposed bounds. Their native fit is unproven. The numeric choices receive this scoped vote; the exact byte-size interpretation must be repaired under EX-G6-F1 before source approval.
designReasons.EX-D8: Unit only as statement result prevents meaningless data inhabitants; registry-owned ordinary/financial classification prevents direct assignment to financial fields at this layer. Complete profile classification and financial footprint reconciliation remain necessary.

coverage.derivationAssessment: All listed local arithmetic, types, values and node counts are consistent with the intended mathematical rules, including 80 constructor pairs and combined staging/strictness/indexing/Quantity/Unit/financial-write examples. This is independent manual derivation inspection, not Core execution or a proof. Exact admission for finite-record-bound cannot be established until EX-G6-F1 is resolved; its 2177/2178/4355 value-node arithmetic is correct. Other fixtures are small schematic terms with assumed valid spans and environments, not hostile-input or serialized-codec tests.
coverage.operandAndTypingAssessment: All 40 have named metadata/evaluated operands, a unique admitted overload or static rejection, and declared result types. Scalar and indexed numeric overloads, collection capacities, nominal records/enums and statement-only Unit are explicit. Quantities reject negative derived scale, exponent overflow and excess symbols; no floating point or coercion.
coverage.framesAndErrorsAssessment: Pure expressions leave frames unchanged. Let extends earlier locals; NextWrite stages one ordinary field using immutable pre; Emit appends ordered descriptors. Whole-action static rejection precedes reduction; runtime uses entered-node left-to-right first failure with rollback. Ensure suffix post reads and unchanged unwritten fields preserve inherited staging. Span/path/work conventions are specified at the mathematical level, but byte-bound failure remains representation-dependent under F1.
coverage.retainedCandidate04: Inspected retained C04-F1 and the full retained blocking review inventory, plus candidate04 type/wire and constructor sections. The new 40 rows address the missing-signature direction but cannot close C04-F1 financial equations or other retained findings.
